coach.charts.volume.title: Weekly volume
coach.charts.volume.definition: Total kilometres run each week over the last 4 ISO weeks (Mon-Sun). Indicator of training load and consistency.
coach.charts.volume.calculation: Sum of run distances per ISO week. Bar highlighted on the peak week.
coach.charts.pace.title: Average pace
coach.charts.pace.definition: Weekly average running pace in min/km. Y-axis is reversed so lower (faster) appears at the top. Helps spot drift week to week.
coach.charts.pace.calculation: Total moving time / total distance per ISO week, running activities only. Dashed line = 4-week average.
coach.charts.intervalPace.title: Interval pace
coach.charts.intervalPace.definition: Average pace during detected interval / fartlek work segments. Lower = faster intervals = better top-end fitness.
coach.charts.intervalPace.calculation: Mean of work-rep paces from interval sessions, last 20 sessions. Y-axis reversed.
coach.charts.efPace.title: Easy pace
coach.charts.efPace.definition: Pace of easy / aerobic runs. Combined with heart rate, reveals aerobic development: pace down + HR stable means improving fitness.
coach.charts.efPace.calculation: Mean pace of easy-endurance runs, last 20 sessions. Y-axis reversed. HR badge = average heart rate over the same runs.
coach.charts.efPace.aerobicHint: Pace down + HR stable = aerobic progress
coach.charts.insights.title: Trend insights
coach.charts.insights.definition: Auto-generated observations from your last 4 weeks of data. Computed client-side from the values shown above.
coach.charts.insights.calculation: Thresholds: volume +/-15% week-1 vs week-4, pace +/-5s/km, ramp rate >10% flagged as high.

metrics.ctl.label: CTL
metrics.ctl.title: Chronic Training Load
metrics.ctl.definition: A rolling estimate of long-term fitness, representing how much training load you have absorbed over the past several weeks.
metrics.ctl.calculation: Exponentially-weighted moving average of daily training load (typically TSS) with a 42-day time constant.
metrics.atl.label: ATL
metrics.atl.title: Acute Training Load
metrics.atl.definition: A rolling estimate of short-term fatigue, representing the training load accumulated in the last week or so.
metrics.atl.calculation: Exponentially-weighted moving average of daily training load (typically TSS) with a 7-day time constant.
metrics.tsb.label: Form
metrics.tsb.title: Training Stress Balance
metrics.tsb.definition: The balance between fitness and fatigue, used as a proxy for race-day freshness. Positive = fresh, negative = fatigued.
metrics.tsb.calculation: Computed as CTL minus ATL, usually using yesterday's values.
metrics.ramp.label: Ramp
metrics.ramp.title: CTL Ramp Rate
metrics.ramp.definition: How fast your fitness (CTL) is rising week over week. A guard-rail against overtraining.
metrics.ramp.calculation: Difference between current CTL and CTL 7 days ago; sustainable range is 3-7 TSS/week.
metrics.tss.label: TSS
metrics.tss.title: Training Stress Score
metrics.tss.definition: A single number quantifying the overall stress of one workout, calibrated so 1 hour at threshold equals 100.
metrics.tss.calculation: Computed from intensity factor and duration: TSS = (sec * NP * IF) / (FTP * 3600) * 100.
metrics.decoupling.label: Decoupling
metrics.decoupling.title: Aerobic Decoupling
metrics.decoupling.definition: How much your heart rate drifts upward at the same pace during a steady aerobic effort. Lower = better aerobic fitness.
metrics.decoupling.calculation: Compare pace-to-HR ratio of the first vs. second half of the run; under 5% is considered coupled.
metrics.hrv.label: HRV
metrics.hrv.title: Heart Rate Variability
metrics.hrv.definition: The natural variation in time between heartbeats, used as a marker of recovery and nervous system balance.
metrics.hrv.calculation: Measured at rest as RMSSD or SDNN in milliseconds from R-R intervals.
metrics.vo2max.label: VO2max
metrics.vo2max.title: Maximal Oxygen Uptake
metrics.vo2max.definition: The maximum amount of oxygen your body can use per minute. The reference marker of aerobic capacity.
metrics.vo2max.calculation: Measured in a lab via gas exchange, or estimated by wearables from running pace and heart rate.
metrics.restinghr.label: Resting HR
metrics.restinghr.title: Resting Heart Rate
metrics.restinghr.definition: Your heart rate measured at complete rest. A trending downward value reflects improving cardiovascular fitness.
metrics.restinghr.calculation: Lowest sustained HR over a few minutes at rest, measured with a chest strap, watch, or manual pulse count.
metrics.sleep.label: Sleep
metrics.sleep.title: Sleep Duration & Quality
metrics.sleep.definition: Total sleep time and its restorative quality, the single biggest lever for adaptation and recovery.
metrics.sleep.calculation: Tracked by wearables combining accelerometer, HR and HRV; adults need 7-9 hours.
metrics.ef.label: EF
metrics.ef.title: Efficiency Factor
metrics.ef.definition: Ratio of pace to heart rate during steady aerobic work. Rising EF means same HR but faster pace - pure aerobic gains.
metrics.ef.calculation: Normalised pace divided by average HR; tracked across easy and long runs to spot trends.
metrics.confidence.label: Confidence
metrics.confidence.title: AI Coach Confidence
metrics.confidence.definition: A 0-1 score on every generated description reflecting how strongly the model trusts its workout interpretation.
metrics.confidence.calculation: Computed from pace consistency: min(0.95, 0.6 + (1 - pace_std) * 0.3), then carried through content generation.
metrics.editrate.label: Edit rate
metrics.editrate.title: User Modification Rate
metrics.editrate.definition: Share of AI-generated descriptions that the user edits before saving. Lower is better - the AI is converging on your voice.
metrics.editrate.calculation: Nightly job compares enhanced vs final description with SequenceMatcher; below 99.5% similarity counts as modified.
metrics.similarity.label: Similarity
metrics.similarity.title: AI / Final Similarity
metrics.similarity.definition: Closeness between the AI-generated description and your final version on Strava, on a 0-1 scale. 1.0 means untouched.
metrics.similarity.calculation: difflib SequenceMatcher ratio on lowercased strings; >= 0.995 means activity not flagged as modified.
metrics.feedbackAnalyzed.label: Feedback analyzed
metrics.feedbackAnalyzed.title: Activities with analyzed user feedback
metrics.feedbackAnalyzed.definition: Number of activities where your edits to the AI-generated description were processed and learned from. Higher = more learning material for the coach AI.
metrics.feedbackAnalyzed.calculation: Count of activities where feedback_analyzed flag is true (post user edit + delta computation).
metrics.memoryLearning.label: Memory
metrics.memoryLearning.title: Learning signal for the AI coach
metrics.memoryLearning.definition: How your interaction with this activity contributed to the AI coach's long-term memory. Edited descriptions teach your style. Kept descriptions reinforce the model as a positive signal. Pending = feedback not yet processed.
metrics.memoryLearning.calculation: Based on feedback_analyzed and description_modified flags. AgentCore Memory observations are written when both signals are present.
metrics.compliance.label: Plan compliance
metrics.compliance.title: Campus Coach plan compliance
metrics.compliance.definition: Completed Campus Coach sessions divided by planned sessions for the current ISO week. 100% means you finished every session of your plan.
metrics.compliance.calculation: completed_sessions / planned_sessions for the current week, expressed as a percentage.
metrics.nextSession.label: Next session
metrics.nextSession.title: AI-recommended next session
metrics.nextSession.definition: Next session recommended by your AI coach based on your latest activity, your Campus Coach weekly plan (when available), and your training load.
metrics.activities.title: Total Activities
metrics.activities.definition: Number of Strava activities processed by the AI coach since you connected.
metrics.successRate.title: Success Rate
metrics.successRate.definition: Percentage of activities successfully enhanced by the AI without errors or timeouts.
metrics.completed.title: Completed
metrics.completed.definition: Activities that received a full AI-generated title and description and were pushed back to Strava.
metrics.avgProcessing.title: Avg Processing Time
metrics.avgProcessing.definition: Average time between webhook reception and Strava update, including module fetches (Enduraw, Campus Coach, Intervals.icu).
metrics.volume.title: Weekly Volume
metrics.volume.definition: Total distance run in the last 7 days across all activities.
metrics.sessions.title: Sessions
metrics.sessions.definition: Number of training sessions in the last 7 days, broken down by activity type.
metrics.thisWeek.title: This Week
metrics.thisWeek.definition: Distance covered since Monday of the current ISO week.
config.strava.section.help.title: Why connect Strava
config.strava.section.help.definition: Strava is the source of truth for your activities. Connecting it lets the AI read your runs to enrich descriptions, track trends, and feed your coach.
config.strava.section.help.calculation: Read-only by default. You can revoke access anytime from your Strava settings.
config.strava.help.title: Strava app setup
config.strava.help.definition: You need to register Strava AI Boost as a personal Strava app. This gives you Client ID and Client Secret used to talk to the Strava API on your behalf.
config.strava.help.calculation: Go to strava.com/settings/api, create an app, set callback domain to localhost, then paste both keys here.
config.strava.clientId.help.title: Strava Client ID
config.strava.clientId.help.definition: Public identifier of your Strava app. Found at strava.com/settings/api after creating an app. Safe to share, used in OAuth redirects.
config.strava.clientSecret.help.title: Strava Client Secret
config.strava.clientSecret.help.definiti: Private key for your Strava app. Used to securely exchange your authorization for access tokens.
config.strava.clientSecret.help.calculat: Stored encrypted server-side. Never sent to the browser after save.
config.testConnection.help.title: Test connection
config.testConnection.help.definition: Calls the Strava API with your stored token to confirm it still works. Returns your athlete ID if healthy.
config.testConnection.help.calculation: Run this if descriptions stop generating - it surfaces token expiry or revoked access.
config.modules.section.help.title: Optional modules
config.modules.section.help.definition: Add-ons that enrich your activity descriptions and coach feedback with extra data sources. All optional and can be enabled independently.
config.module.campus.help.title: Campus Coach
config.module.campus.help.definition: Pulls your Campus Coach training plan so the AI can match each Strava activity to a planned session and report compliance vs intent.
config.module.campus.help.calculation: Sessions are scraped daily. Compliance = completed / planned for the current ISO week.
config.module.campus.credentials.help.de: Login used to scrape your weekly plan from app.campus.coach. Your credentials never leave the encrypted secret store.
config.module.intervals.help.title: Intervals.icu
config.module.intervals.help.definition: Pulls fitness load metrics (CTL, ATL, Form, Ramp, HRV, VO2max, resting HR) so the coach reads your training in context, not just one workout at a time.
config.module.intervals.help.calculation: Data refreshed before each activity processing. Falls back gracefully if Intervals.icu is unreachable.
config.module.intervals.apiKey.help.defi: Personal token from intervals.icu Settings > Developer Settings. Read-only access to your athlete data.
config.module.intervals.apiKey.help.calc: Stored encrypted server-side. Rotate it on intervals.icu anytime, then update here.
config.module.enduraw.help.title: Enduraw
config.module.enduraw.help.definition: Adds weather, wind, and terrain impact to each activity. Lets the AI explain a slow pace by a 30 km/h headwind rather than blaming your fitness.
config.module.enduraw.help.calculation: Activities wait up to 2 minutes for Enduraw data; generation continues without it on timeout.
preferences.profile.help.title: Athlete profile
preferences.profile.help.definition: Free-form description of your goals, training history, injuries, racing background. The AI uses it to personalize titles and coach feedback to your reality.
preferences.profile.help.calculation: Injected into every AI prompt as system context. Keep it updated as your goals shift.
preferences.profile.field.help.title: What to write here
preferences.profile.field.help.definitio: The more specific, the better. Mention target races, weekly volume, weak spots, recent injuries, and what you want the coach to focus on.
preferences.profile.field.help.calculati: Up to 2000 characters. Plain text, no formatting needed.
preferences.maxHr.help.title: Maximum heart rate
preferences.maxHr.help.definition: Your peak heart rate. Used by the coach to compute zone percentages (%HRmax) and detect overload in feedback.
preferences.maxHr.help.calculation: Tanaka formula estimates 208 - 0.7 x age. Override with a field test or recent max effort for accuracy.
preferences.records.help.title: Personal records
preferences.records.help.definition: Your benchmark times on standard distances. The coach uses them to contextualize current fitness and gauge race readiness.
preferences.records.help.calculation: Mixed with Strava best efforts when available. Older PRs are weighted lower in coach reasoning.
preferences.zones.help.title: Pace zones
preferences.zones.help.definition: Boundaries that classify each run as Recovery, EF, Tempo, Threshold, or VO2max. Drives session labeling and pace-progression charts.
preferences.zones.help.calculation: Defaults are conservative estimates. Tune them based on your latest threshold test or race performance.
preferences.style.help.title: Content style
preferences.style.help.definition: Controls how the AI writes your activity descriptions: length, tone, emoji density, technical depth, and language.
preferences.style.help.calculation: These knobs shape every generated title and report. Change them anytime - applies to future activities.
preferences.style.length.help.title: Description length
preferences.style.length.help.definition: How long each activity description should be. Short = key metrics only. Detailed = full analysis. Adaptive scales with workout complexity.
preferences.style.tone.help.title: Tone
preferences.style.tone.help.definition: Voice the AI uses: technical, motivational, casual, humorous, or authentic. Sets the personality of every description.
preferences.style.emoji.help.title: Emoji usage
preferences.style.emoji.help.definition: How many emojis appear in generated text. None for clean output, enthusiastic for high-energy posts.
preferences.style.technical.help.title: Technical detail
preferences.style.technical.help.definit: Depth of metrics in descriptions. Basic = pace and distance. Advanced = HR zones, splits, decoupling, stream-level analysis.
preferences.style.language.help.title: Content language
preferences.style.language.help.definiti: Language used for generated titles and descriptions on Strava. Independent of the app UI language.
preferences.demographics.help.title: Demographics
preferences.demographics.help.definition: Optional context the AI uses to adapt cultural references, vocabulary, and tone to your generation and motivation profile.
preferences.demographics.age.help.title: Age range
preferences.demographics.age.help.defini: Helps the AI calibrate references, training advice, and tone. Also used as fallback to estimate max HR via Tanaka formula.
preferences.demographics.sportApproach.h: Your main reason for training. Performance-focused gets data-heavy feedback; wellness-focused gets supportive, balanced framing.
Topics outside running that the AI can weave into descriptions for personality. Optional - empty is fine.
empty.records.title: No records yet
